title: Druze leader Fouad Jumblatt shot dead
why: Early political killing under the French Mandate; the list names Shakeeb Wahhab as the shooter.

title: Syrian ex-head of state Sami al-Hinnawi shot in Beirut
why: Syrian political rivalry reached Beirut; the list names Hersho al-Barazi as the shooter.

title: Journalist Nasib al-Matni shot in West Beirut office
why: Nasserist journalist shot in his office months before the 1958 civil clashes, per the list.

title: MP Naim Moghabghab shot dead
why: Post-1958 political violence; the list attributes the shooting to the Progressive Socialist Party.

title: Publisher Kamel Mrowa shot in his office
why: Newspaper publisher shot at the Al-Hayat office in Beirut; the shooter is named as Adnan Sultani, who was convicted and sentenced to 20 years; investigators linked the killing to the Independent Nasserite Movement.

title: Syrian defence minister Muhammad Umran shot outside Tripoli home
why: Shot outside his home in Tripoli after fleeing to Lebanon; the case is unsolved.

title: Palestinian writer Ghassan Kanafani killed by Beirut car bomb
why: PFLP spokesman killed; the list attributes the attack to Mossad.

title: Linda Jumblatt, Kamal Jumblatt's sister, shot in Beirut
why: Killed in an East Beirut apartment during the civil war.

title: Kataeb figure Joud el-Bayeh killed in Zgharta area
why: Kataeb leader killed six days before the Ehden massacre; the list attributes it to the Marada Movement.

title: Journalist Salim Lawzi's body found after kidnapping and torture
why: Kidnapped 25 Feb 1980; body found 4 Mar 1980 bearing signs of torture; widely suspected to be the work of Syrian intelligence, but killers were never officially identified. (corrected from date shown is body discovery; kill date unknown)

title: Iraqi-Iranian Shia scholar Hassan al-Shirazi shot in Beirut
why: The list attributes the killing to Ba'ath officers.

title: French ambassador Louis Delamare shot at a checkpoint
why: Diplomat killed in Beirut; the list gives no perpetrator.

title: PLO commander Saad Sayel shot dead in ambush near Syrian border
why: Convoy ambushed between Talia and Safri villages on 29 Sep 1982; died of wounds in a Damascus hospital; the Abu Nidal Organization claimed responsibility, though some sources suggest Israeli intelligence. (corrected from place Beirut)

title: Shia leader Ragheb Harb shot in the south
why: Shia cleric and resistance leader killed at Jibchit, south Lebanon; the article names assassins incl. Hussein Abbas and cites an unverified admission by Danny Abdallah.

title: CIA officer William Buckley reported executed in captivity
why: Hostage held since March 1984; the list says the Islamic Jihad Organization executed him.

title: Islamic Unification Movement leader Khalil Akkawi shot
why: Islamic Unification Movement leader killed; the list attributes it to Syrian military intelligence.

title: Marxist thinker Husayn Muruwwa shot dead
why: Shot in his bed at home in Beirut by two armed men posing as Communist Party messengers; perpetrators never charged or identified.

title: Marxist intellectual Mahdi Amel shot dead
why: Communist theorist shot on Algeria Street, per the list.

title: Sunni Higher Council head Sobhi Saleh shot near mosque
why: Head of the Sunni Islamic Higher Council shot near a West Beirut mosque; Mufti Khaled was killed two weeks later.

title: Hezbollah chief Abbas al-Musawi killed by Israeli helicopters
why: Israeli Apache fire on his motorcade killed him, his wife, son and four others; Nasrallah succeeded him.

title: Former foreign minister Henri Pharaon killed at Beirut hotel; ex-bodyguard arrested
why: Stabbed 16 times in his room at the Carlton Hotel; his driver and bodyguard were also found stabbed to death; a former bodyguard was arrested and police suggested robbery. (corrected from deaths 1 and "stabbed by ex-bodyguard" stated as fact)

title: Al-Ahbash leader Nizar al-Halabi shot dead
why: Sufi-Sunni movement head killed; the list names Osbat al-Ansar members.

title: SLA colonel Aql Hashem killed by remote bomb
why: The list attributes the bomb to Hezbollah.

title: PFLP-GC leader Jihad Jibril killed by car bomb
why: The list attributes the attack to Mossad.

title: Amal official Ghaleb Awwali killed by car bomb
why: Killed by car bomb on 19 Jul 2004 in Beirut; Hezbollah blamed Israel and Jund al-Sham without evidence, while others suspected Hezbollah itself.

title: Deputy PM Elias Murr survives Antelias bomb
why: One killed and 12 injured; the STL later judged this attack connected to the Hariri case.

title: TV host May Chidiac loses limbs in Jounieh car bomb
why: Attack on an outspoken critic of Syria; she lost a leg and an arm and survived.

title: Islamic Jihad official Mahmoud al-Majzoub killed in Sidon
why: Car bomb in Sidon killed him and his brother Nidal; Islamic Jihad, Hezbollah and the Lebanese government blamed Israel, which denied it; Lebanese authorities later arrested alleged spy suspects.

title: Lebanese Democratic Party figure Saleh al-Aridi killed by car bomb
why: Aley district bombing per the list.

title: Hezbollah commander Hassan al-Laqqis shot dead
why: Shot outside his home in Hadath, Beirut suburbs, around 3-4 Dec 2013; the Ahrar al-Sunna Baalbek Brigade claimed it; Hezbollah blamed Israel, which denied involvement. (corrected from perpetrator wording)

title: Security chief Abbas Ibrahim survives assassination attempt
why: General Security head targeted at a Dahr al-Baydar checkpoint, per the Al Jazeera timeline.

title: Retired customs anti-smuggling official Mounir Abou Rjeily found dead at home in Qartaba
why: Found dead at his home on the morning of 2 Dec 2020 after being struck on the head; investigators named no suspects. Some later claims (e.g. by Israeli military intelligence) allege other motives; unproven. (corrected from place Beirut; "stabbed" not in HRW)

title: Radwan commander Wissam al-Tawil killed in Israeli strike
why: Hezbollah Radwan commander killed in an Israeli airstrike, days after the Arouri strike.

title: Lebanese Forces coordinator Pascal Suleiman killed
why: Lebanese Forces coordinator shot dead; the list names a Syrian gang.

title: Hezbollah missiles unit chief Ibrahim Qobeissy killed
why: Hezbollah missiles unit leader killed in an Israeli airstrike during the September 2024 campaign.

title: Ali Karaki and IRGC general Nilforoushan killed with Nasrallah
why: Both named as killed in the 27 Sep 2024 Israeli strike on Hezbollah headquarters in Dahieh with Nasrallah; Lebanese health ministry counted at least 33 dead by 28 Sep.

title: Hezbollah executive council deputy Nabil Qaouk killed
why: Deputy head of Hezbollah's executive council killed in an Israeli airstrike a day after Nasrallah.

title: Israeli strike on Hashem Safieddine in Dahieh
why: Date of the strike per the list; Hezbollah confirmed his death on 22 October.
dup_of: Hezbollah confirms Hashem Safieddine killed in Israeli strike

title: Hezbollah spokesman Mohammad Afif killed in Beirut
why: Hezbollah spokesman killed at the Ba'ath Party headquarters in Beirut, per the list.

title: Hamas commander Mohammed Shaheen killed in Israeli strike
why: Al-Qassam Brigades leader killed in an Israeli airstrike during the post-2024 ceasefire period.

title: Quds Force commanders killed in Lebanon strikes
why: Wikipedia's 2026 war chronology lists Iranian Quds Force commanders among those killed on 8 March.

title: Ain Ebel massacre
why: Early Mandate-era violence in the south; sources vary on toll.

title: Battle of Rashaya: Druze rebels besiege French garrison during Great Syrian Revolt
why: 20-24 Nov 1925; stories of massacres of local Christians accompanied the revolt, with 429 Christian homes damaged or destroyed in Rashaya (corrected from "Rashaya massacre", "hundreds" killed).
deaths: about 400 rebels killed or wounded; 58 French casualties

title: Tripoli student demonstrators killed
why: Students shot in Tripoli in November 1943; the list gives 14 dead and attributes it to French-Senegalese soldiers.

title: Hula massacre by Israeli forces
why: Killings of civilians at Hula in the 1948 war; the list attributes them to the IDF, with tolls of 34-89.

title: Miziara massacre
why: Intra-Maronite clan killings in the north.

title: Black Thursday killings in Beirut
why: Series of sectarian killings in the opening phase of the civil war.

title: Beit Mellat massacre
why: Killings in Beit Mellat, per the list.

title: Chekka massacre
why: Attributed by the list to LNM/PLO forces.

title: Tel al-Zaatar massacre
why: Camp fell after a 52-day siege; toll sources range widely.

title: Aishiyeh massacre
why: Killings in Aishiyeh, 19-21 October 1976; the list gives 70 or more dead.

title: Chouf massacres after Jumblatt's assassination
why: Killings of civilians in the Chouf, 16-30 March 1977, after Kamal Jumblatt's assassination; the list attributes them to the PLA.

title: Brih church attack
why: Attack on St George's Church in Brih; the list attributes it to the PLA.

title: Qaa massacre
why: 28 Jun 1978 killings in four Baalbek-district villages, attributed to the Marada Brigade and Defense Companies as retaliation for the Ehden massacre; 26 killed, about 40 reportedly kidnapped.

title: Kfarmatta massacre
why: Druze civilians killed after Christian forces took Kfarmatta; the article attributes it to Phalangist militias and the Lebanese Army; early reports said up to 40, 117 bodies found when the village was retaken. (corrected from attribution)

title: Southern Mount Lebanon massacres of the Mountain War
why: The list dates this 1984 but the Mountain War ran September 1983; toll per list.

title: Sohmor massacre
why: Killings at Sohmor; the list attributes them to the South Lebanon Army.

title: Dahr al-Wahsh massacre
why: Killings at Dahr al-Wahsh at the end of the civil war; the list attributes them to the Syrian army.

title: Mansouri attack
why: 13 Apr 1996: Israeli helicopter missiles hit an ambulance in Mansouri, killing six (two women, four children); Israel said it was used by fighters; Amnesty found no Hezbollah link.

title: Nabatieh Fawka attack
why: 16 Apr 1996: Israeli helicopter rockets destroyed a house, killing nine (seven children); Israel cited Hezbollah activity; Amnesty and HRW found no evidence of it.

title: Qana shelling toll and aftermath (Grapes of Wrath)
why: Israeli shelling of a UN compound killed about 105 civilians; the massacres list gives 106.
dup_of: Israeli shelling of Qana UN base

title: Marjayoun convoy air strike near Kefraya
why: 11 Aug 2006: Israeli air strike on a convoy leaving Marjayoun, near Kefraya in the Bekaa; 7 killed, 36 injured; Israel later called it a mistake. (corrected from place and location name (Kfar Kila))

title: Ainata airstrike kills civilians
why: Israeli airstrike on Ainata killed four, per the list.

title: Nabatieh strike
why: Israeli airstrike in Nabatieh; 11 or more killed per the list.

title: Israeli strike on Beirut medical center
why: 4 Oct 2024: strike on an Islamic Health Organization medical centre in Bashoura; at least 9 killed, 14+ injured; Israel said it housed Hezbollah assets.

title: Derdghaya Melkite church-area airstrike
why: Israeli airstrike on Derdghaya; 8 or more killed per the list.

title: Bachoura airstrike in central Beirut
why: 10 Oct 2024: strike on residential buildings in Bachoura; at least 22 killed and 117 injured per the health ministry.

title: Aitou airstrike kills 21-23
why: 14 Oct 2024: strike on a building housing displaced families in Aitou, Zgharta; tolls of 21 to 23 reported.

title: Strike on Nabatieh municipal council
why: Israeli strike on Nabatieh's municipal council; 16 or more killed per the list.

title: Beqaa Valley airstrikes
why: 28 Oct 2024: strikes on about a dozen Beqaa settlements, at least 60 killed that day; the article gives 134+ across the 28 Oct-6 Nov series.

title: Barja airstrike
why: Israeli strike on a residential building in Barja, Chouf, on the evening of 5 Nov 2024; tolls range from 20 (LBC) to at least 35 (The National) (corrected from 2024-11-07).

title: Akkar airstrike at Ain Yaaqoub
why: 11 Nov 2024: strike on a residential building in Ain Yaaqoub, Akkar; at least 14 killed and 15 injured. (corrected from toll 15+)

title: Basta airstrikes in Beirut
why: Israeli airstrikes on Basta, Beirut; 29 or more killed per the list.

title: Bint Jbeil drone strike
why: 21 Sep 2025: Israeli drone strikes killed five, incl. three children; Israel said it targeted a Hezbollah operative.

title: Israeli strike on Ain al-Hilweh camp, Sidon
why: 18 Nov 2025: strike on Ain al-Hilweh killed at least 13, incl. 11 children; Israel said it targeted a Hamas training compound, which Hamas denied; deadliest single strike since the Nov 2024 ceasefire.

title: 8 April 2026 Israeli attacks: toll in the list
why: Lebanese health ministry: 357 killed and 1,223 wounded across Beirut and other areas; Israel said it hit Hezbollah targets and claimed 180-250 militants killed.

title: Israeli forces enter south Lebanon in Operation Hiram
why: Incursion into southern Lebanon during the final phase of the 1948 war; an armistice followed on 23 March 1949.

title: Four Iranian diplomats seized, start of the hostage era
why: Kidnapped on 5 July 1982; the page attributes the seizure to Phalangist militia.

title: CIA officer William Buckley kidnapped in Beirut
why: Captured in March 1984; he died in captivity in June 1985 per the hostage crisis page.

title: AP reporter Terry Anderson seized in Beirut
why: Held until December 1991, the longest-held American hostage.

title: British journalist John McCarthy kidnapped
why: Held until August 1991.

title: AUB administrator Joseph Cicippio kidnapped
why: Held 1,908 days according to the page.

title: Israeli commandos seize Sheikh Abdul Karim Obeid in Jibchit
why: Hezbollah responded by announcing the execution of UNIFIL officer Col. William Higgins.

title: Last Western hostages freed, ending the hostage crisis
why: Two German relief workers released; the crisis spanned 1982-1992 with 104 foreign hostages and at least 8 deaths in captivity.

title: Israeli commandos abduct Amal figure Mustafa Dirani
why: The abduction preceded an Israeli airstrike on a Hezbollah training camp that killed 30-45 cadets.

title: Israeli airstrike on a Hezbollah training camp
why: Strike after the Dirani abduction killed 30-45 cadets per the page; exact date not given there.

title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire understanding ends Grapes of Wrath
why: Took effect 27 April 1996 at 04:00, banning attacks on civilian targets; a five-party monitoring group was set up.

title: Grapes of Wrath: toll as stated
why: Lebanese civilians killed 149-250 by source; 350,000-500,000 displaced; ran to 27 April.
dup_of: Israel launches Operation Grapes of Wrath

title: Operation Accountability: toll as stated
why: 25-31 July 1993: 140 Lebanese civilians killed; about 300,000 displaced; oral understanding brokered by the US.

title: Ansariya ambush kills 12 Israeli naval commandos
why: Hezbollah ambush on 4-5 September 1997; a Lebanese woman and girl also died in the crossfire.

title: Israeli strikes hit Lebanese power stations
why: 24-25 Jun 1999 Israeli air raids after Hezbollah rocket fire hit the Jamhour power plant (Beirut blackout), a telephone HQ and the al-Manar station; about $52 million damage; 8 Lebanese killed, 70 seriously injured (date refined from 1999-06).

title: Dinnieh clashes: army fights Islamist militants
why: Army fought the Takfir wa al-Hijra group until 6 January 2000; 12 soldiers and 25 militants killed.

title: Hariri truck bomb: toll and later convictions
why: 22 killed and 220 wounded; STL convicted Salim Ayyash in 2020 and Merhi and Oneissi in 2022.
dup_of: Rafic Hariri killed by Beirut truck bomb

title: Twin bus bombings near Bikfaya
why: Two buses blasted near Ain Alaq; three killed and 21 injured; the page names Fatah al-Islam.

title: Hezbollah raid near Zar'it triggers the 2006 war
why: Three Israeli soldiers killed and two captured; five more died in a rescue attempt.

title: 2006 war ceasefire takes effect
why: The war ran 12 July-14 August; 1,191-1,300 Lebanese and 165 Israelis killed; blockade lifted 8 September.

title: Israel lifts naval blockade, formally ending the 2006 war
why: The page gives 8 September as the war's formal conclusion.

title: Tripoli bus bomb kills soldiers and civilians
why: Bomb on an army bus; tolls reported from 11 to 18 killed; Fatah al-Islam was suspected.

title: Car bomb in Bir el-Abed injures 53
why: No deaths; the 313 Brigade claimed it and an FSA spokesman denied involvement.

title: Haret Hreik explosion kills at least four
why: One of nine attacks on Hezbollah areas between July 2013 and February 2014.

title: Hermel suicide blast claimed by Nusra Front
why: Petrol-station suicide attack killed at least four.

title: Bekaa suicide car bomb kills Hezbollah figure Abdul Rahman al-Qadhi
why: At least four killed.

title: Kahaleh clash after Hezbollah truck overturns
why: Two men were shot dead, Fadi al-Bajani and Hezbollah member Ahmad Qasat; the army seized munitions.

title: STL opens first trial in The Hague
why: First trial began 16 January 2014 in the Hariri case.

title: STL ends proceedings against Mustafa Badreddine
why: He died on 13 May 2016; the tribunal terminated proceedings on 12 July.

title: STL appeals conclude; Merhi and Oneissi convicted
why: Appeals concluded in 2022; the Hariri page says Merhi and Oneissi were also convicted that year.

title: Special Tribunal for Lebanon closes
why: The tribunal closed on 31 December 2023 after investigations and trials costing nearly $1 billion.

title: Israel-Lebanon 10-day ceasefire begins
why: US-mediated ceasefire took effect 16 April 2026 with a mutual extension clause.

title: Ceasefire extended three weeks
why: Extension announced by US President Trump.

title: Ceasefire extended 45 days
why: Further extension; Hezbollah rejected several later framework proposals.
